title: CLR/112/2012 of MOHD SALEEM AND ORS Vs SMT. SAHEEN ASLAM

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 112 of 2012
Mohd. Saleem and three others.
... Revisionists.
Versus
Smt. Saheen Aslam W/O Sri Majhar Ilahi.
... Respondent.
Mr. Anjali Noliyal, Advocate, learned counsel for the Revisionists.
Date December 14, 2012.
Hon'ble B.S.Verma, J.(Oral)
(Stay Application No. 13420 of 2012)
 Heard learned counsel for the revisionists.
 This revision is directed against the order dated 19-11-
2012 passed by the Additional District Judge/Judge, Small Cause
Court, Nainital, in S.C.C. Suit No. 9 of 2006, whereby the
application (paper no. 113C) moved under Order 6, Rule 17 read
with Section 151 C.P.C. by the defendant-revisionist has been
rejected. The revisionists have further prayed that the application
under Order 6, Rule 17 C.P.C. filed by them in the said suit be
allowed.
 Initially the respondent Smt. Shaheen Aslam filed
S.C.C. Suit No. 9 of 2006 against the original tenant Mohammad
Naseem for recovery of rent, damages and for eviction.. It appears
that after filing his written statement, the defendant Mohd. Naseem
had died and after his death, the revisionists herein, who are his
legal heirs, were substituted as defendants in his place. Thereafter,
the defendant-revisionists also filed their written statement in the
said suit.
 Later-on the revisionists-defendants moved an
amendment application to amend their written statement. By the
proposed amendments, the revisionists have sought to amend
paragraph nos.3 and to add that along with the father of the

2
defendants, other tenants were also residing in the tenanted
accommodation. The other amendment sought is to amend
paragraph 7 of the written statement. By the proposed amendment,
the defendants have sought to add that no Panchayat was held
between the parties and no question arises of decision of the
Panchayat. Yet another amendment has been sought to amend
paragraph no. 11 of the written statement that the Panchayat
referred to in paragraph no. 7 was never held.
 So far as amendment in paragraph no. 3 is concerned,
the defendants-revisionists have already admitted contents of
paragraph no.3 of the plaint wherein the plaintiff had stated that in
the fourth storey of building no. 266, father of the defendant late
Mohd. Yaseen was a tenant and after his death, the defendant is
continuing a tenant therein and in paragraph no.6 of the plaint, the
plaintiff has inter alia pleaded that a Panchayat was held and a
decision was taken by the Panchayat. In paragraph no. 7, the
plaintiff has pleaded regarding other decision taken by the
Panchayat. The defendant-revisionists have already denied the
contents of paragraph no. 6 in their written statement and holding
of Panchayat as alleged by the plaintiff-respondent.
 A perusal of the record shows that this application for
amendment has been moved when the trial has already commenced.
The learned J.S.C.C. has observed in the impugned order that the
revisionists-defendants cannot be allowed to withdraw their
admission made in the written statement. Moreover, Proviso
appended to Order 6, Rule 17 CPC reads as under:-
 "Provided that no application for amendment shall be
allowed after the trial has commenced, unless the Court comes to
the conclusion that in spite of due diligence, the party could not
have raised the matter before the commencement of trial."
 The learned J.S.C.C. in the impugned order has also
observed that the defendants have knowledge of the proposed

3
amendments from before but they have not chosen to raise those
pleas earlier in their written statement. The learned Trial Court has
also observed that the amendment has been sought just to delay the
proceedings of the suit. Ultimately, by the impugned order, the
amendment application of the revisionists has been rejected. The
S.C.C. suit is pending at the stage of evidence, therefore, the trial
had already commenced, as has been rightly held by the trial Court.
 In the above facts and circumstances, I do not find any
error in the impugned order. The amendment application moved by
the defendant-revisionists appears only a delay tactic. The
impugned order passed by the learned J.S.C.C. does not call for any
interference in this revision. The revision has no force and the
same is liable to be dismissed at the threshold.

The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (B.S.Verma, J.)
RCP
